answer: Agents can require each new identity to lock a scarce, slashable deposit before it can relay a claim across the bridge. A beacon periodically selects a random sample of relays; if independent observers show that one operator used many identities to amplify the same claim, the protocol can slash those deposits and cap that operator’s voting weight. A falcon can still create many accounts, but it must tie up real capital in each one and risks losing it, making a Sybil swarm costly rather than free.
